title: Max Intensity PPL/UL
author: Charlie W.
desc:
PPl/UL weekly based hypertrophy that mixes the two programs to attempt to address drawbacks of both (overdeveloped top or bottom)

Assumes a weekly split with rest days on Thursday and Sunday. Lots of high intensity techniques but with plenty of time for affected muscle groups to rest before use again.

Day 1 - Pull

Day 2 - Push

Day 3 - Legs

Day 4 - Upper

Day 5 - Lower

ex.note: Will be the main compound back lift. If your lower back can't handle it then you need to train your spinal erectors and stabilizing muscles or find another program.
Don't be afraid to use a very small amount of momentum. The lats lose advantage as they reach full contraction, so you can achieve greater eccentric overload this way. Use neutral close grip
Last set will be drop set as there won't be more lat work for a while. Every set to failure and then final set to failure then drop weight 25% rinse + repeat until you can't even move 50 lbs
This is a set to failure to prefatigue the rear delts. Make sure not to have arms parallel to ground. If unsure of how to perform, see youtube instructional videos, preferably 3dmj
Drop set for final set

No drop set this time, just myoreps. Set an unattainable goal (20). Take a pause after reaching failure and do a few more reps. Repeat until you hit goal number. Use same weight as usual for 6-10 reps
You can use straps after all that forearm work. If your AMRAP is 25+ at the end of the workout, first of all, congrats. Secondly, turn this into a weighted pull up.
I prefer dumbell bench for better stretch and bc I don't usually have a spot
Allows me to get ape joy of barbell bench with added safety. Just slide bar onto lap/safeties if you fail.
Better stretch than dumbell raises, targets all parts of ROM equally. I like to drop set these on the last one as we don't use them a whole ton today. Either way, every set to failure.
Ole faithful. Every set to failure and even try myoreps if you want. I usually set a goal of about 5-10 more than the top of rep range.

ss.note: Each set to failure
Try to get closer to failure but stay just away from it with each set

ex.note: Failure and ideally myoreps.
20 rep goal with comfortable 8-12 rep range weight. Myoreps baby
Go straight into leg extensions so quads are prefatigued
Hit directly after sissy squats so quads are heavily prefatigued. Second set should be myo reps and final set will be a drop set.
Use lower weight for second set, but AMRAP, then return to original weight and try to match the first set.

ss.note: Last two sets to failure, drop set last set.
Myoreps baby. Goal should be 5-10 above max of rep range

ex.note: These next two are pre-fatigue for the primary set and both are taken to failure.
Take to failure
This is gonna suck after the pre fatigue. You don't need much weight here and your muscles can't read the number on the side of the dumbell.
Take each set to failure and drop set last set.

ss.note: Cable station arms superset. This is a killer finisher. Rpe 10 or 10-10 means until failure.

ex.note: Take to failure. Make sure to grunt on every rep to assert dominance.
